basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 12.' and it opens 'Vers. 12. Vagus et profugus eris super terram. Hoc de eis manifestum est qui per omnem'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 12. Vagus et profugus eris super terram. Hoc de eis manifestum est qui per omnem Romani orbis imperium vagi et profugi sunt nec usquam habent certas sedes.
